strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy/scipy#22810 (hyp2f1 extreme inputs): build SciPy at buggy commit 0a21b51926be in a Python 3.12 environment with gcc 12.3.0 and OpenBLAS 0.3.27, then run the developer's new TestHyp2f1ExtremeInputs class. On the buggy build, infinite a or b makes max_degree wrap to 0 via undefined uint64 conversion, so hyp2f1 returns 1+0j instead of nan+nanj and the np.isnan assertions fail. On the fixed revision the same tests pass.

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy && cd scipy && git checkout 0a21b51926be && git submodule update --init
pinned_because: numpy 1.26.4: stated in issue#20988 system info alongside SciPy 1.15.0.dev0+950.c22b657; no documented constraint, so this is the observed version rather than a required one
pythran 0.15.0: stated in issue#20988 build info; not numerically relevant to hyp2f1, pinned only to match the observed build
mpmath unpinned: version not stated in evidence; test file does not appear to need it for the new class, and it is not pinned here

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_hyp2f1.py::TestHyp2f1ExtremeInputs (test_inf_a_b over a,b in {-inf,inf} with z=4.0+1.0j, and test_large_a_b)
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on buggy 0a21b51926be, at least one parametrised case of test_inf_a_b (e.g. a=1.0, b=-inf, c=3.0, z=4+1j) fails because hyp2f1 returns 1+0j, which is not NaN, so np.isnan is False and the assert fails; on the fixed revision (max_degree compared to UINT64_MAX-1 and stored as double) every case of TestHyp2f1ExtremeInputs passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: hyp2f1(1.0, -np.inf, 3.0, 4.0+1.0j) should be nan+nanj on fixed code; buggy code gives 1+0j.
risks: Mechanism is undefined behaviour (casting inf to uint64_t, then unsigned wrap of max_degree+1 and +2). The wrap to 0 depends on how gcc lowers the conversion at the chosen optimisation level. Non-x86 targets, clang, or -fsanitize=undefined builds may give a different buggy value or none at all, so the transition is not guaranteed off this toolchain.

Evidence reports the buggy output only from issue#20988 on main, and v1.13.1 as the reference. The exact buggy output was not verified on 0a21b51926be by the evidence, so the failing assertion is inferred from the code path, not observed.

Test matrix is wide (5x5x4 parametrisation). Some cases with finite a or b are skipped by the guard, so the failing cases are the infinite ones only; if the guard logic differs, the buggy failure could be masked.
test_large_a_b checks 10**7 and -10**7 with complex z; whether these also fail on buggy code is not established by the evidence, so the transition depends mainly on the infinite-input cases.
Numerical reference is the issue's reasoning (nan for infinite parameters), not a verified spec; tests use exact np.isnan checks, so no tolerance applies.
Build requires OpenBLAS discovery via pkgconfig; if the build picks a different BLAS the bug mechanism is unaffected, but build flags were not stated in evidence and are assumed here.
Pythran, pybind11 and mpmath versions are unbounded in the era constraints; the strategy chose the observed numpy 1.26.4 and pythran 0.15.0 and left the others open.

oracle.reference_source: issue#20988 expected nan+nanj and PR#22810 test assertions (np.isnan)
oracle.why: Tests assert NaN via np.isnan, a boolean check with no numerical tolerance, so the oracle is exact on NaN-ness.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 0a21b51926be, hyp2f1(1.0, -inf, 3.0, 4+1j) returns 1+0j because max_degree wraps to 0 and no series terms are summed; np.isnan(1+0j) is False, so the assert in test_inf_a_b raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision max_degree is checked against UINT64_MAX-1 and held as double, so infinite a or b produces NaN, np.isnan is True for every case, and the whole TestHyp2f1ExtremeInputs class passes.
